_meta._comment: Keys beginning with an underscore are metadata, not repositories. Consumers must filter them out before iterating.

1.name: Core Platform & Board Contract
1.hint: Standard hardware driver engine and companion reference code.

2.name: Python Framebuffers & GUI Toolkits
2.hint: Pure Python on any Python 3 host; pygraphics adds native wheels for Linux x86_64, Windows, Android and Pyodide.

3.name: LVGL Native Extensions & Binding Generator
3.hint: Single-source LVGL C header binding generator and native interpreter modules.

4.name: App Hosts & Mobile
4.hint: Deploy PyDevices apps directly to desktop browsers or mobile APKs.

5.name: Developer Tools & Infrastructure
5.hint: MIP package indexing, multi-usermod builds, and serial/FTP IDE extensions.

excluded.android-runner: Exists solely to enable omnipython/bin/android.py. The APK is documented in omnipython; the runner publishes no site.

moved.displayif: now [`modules/displayif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/omnipython-builds/tree/main/modules/displayif) in omnipython-builds. The old repository is archived.
moved.audiocomponents: split into [`audioinstruments`](https://github.com/PyDevices/audioinstruments) and [`audioeffects`](https://github.com/PyDevices/audioeffects). The old repository is archived.
moved.audioif: now [`modules/audioif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/omnipython-builds/tree/main/modules/audioif) in omnipython-builds. The old repository is archived.
moved.cameraif: now [`modules/cameraif`](https://github.com/PyDevices/omnipython-builds/tree/main/modules/cameraif) in omnipython-builds. The old repository is archived.

moved.lvgl-circuitpython: now [`ports/circuitpython`](https://github.com/PyDevices/omnipython-lvgl/tree/main/ports/circuitpython) in omnipython-lvgl. The old repository is archived.

portal_cards._comment: The front page below the hero: try_it is the two doors to try it now, then the cards, first to last, what a new visitor needs first at the top, then the line pointing to the PyDevices tools. A card with 'repo' takes its link and glyph from that repository's entry; one without names its own. Every repository whose portal_grid is not false must be a card.

try_it.heading: Try it now
try_it.hint: Nothing to install, in this browser tab.

doors.title: Watch it run
doors.text: Apps written with OmniPython running in your tab, MicroPython compiled to WebAssembly, with the code that draws them.

doors.title: Write your own in PyDevices Workbench
doors.text: An editor and a simulated board in your browser: write a program, run it on the simulator, then send it to a real board.

portal_cards.heading: The libraries, and where to read about them
portal_cards.hint: The docs and the package library first, then what your program imports, most used first.

cards.name: docs.omnipython.org
cards.text: Install OmniPython on a board, a desktop or in the browser, then the guides and the reference for each library.

cards.name: lib.omnipython.org
cards.text: The package library: every OmniPython package and board driver, installed on a MicroPython board with mip or omip.
The board contract: a small board_config per board, and display, touch, audio and event code that runs the same on all three Pythons.
2D drawing, text and bitmaps: native C where it is built in, pure Python everywhere else.
LVGL 9 for Python: a program imports lvgl the same way on MicroPython, CircuitPython and a desktop.
CircuitPython's audio system (audiocore, synthio, audiomixer, effects) on MicroPython and CPython as well.
Playable synthesizers, organs, electric pianos and drum machines, in pure Python on audiodsp.
Studio and guitar-pedal effects: compressors, EQs, reverbs, delays, drive and amps, in pure Python on audiodsp.
Chris Johnson's 528 Airwindows plug-ins as audio nodes on audiodsp, on MicroPython-compatible firmware and CPython.
Colour wheels, colour cubes, Material Design swatches and RGB565 conversion.
Material Design icons kept in flash, drawn in LVGL or pygraphics.
Builds MicroPython and CircuitPython firmware with OmniPython inside, the desktop interpreters and the WebAssembly runtime.
A starting point for an OmniPython web app that works offline, published on GitHub Pages.
Package an OmniPython app as an Android APK.
Home, Watch and finished apps for music, cameras, the desk and the board, installed on a board with one omip line, and the libraries they share.
A widget toolkit in pure Python, showing that the core can carry a UI framework. For an interface you ship, use LVGL.

portal_cards.tools_line: Looking for the board tool or the audio plug-in? MCU Control and mpvst are made by PyDevices, like Workbench, at pydevices.com.

omnipython.headline: omnipython — Hardware Abstraction Layer & Core Contract.
omnipython.description: Unified pure-Python hardware abstraction layer and core device contract for MicroPython, CircuitPython, CPython, direct WebAssembly, Pyodide, and Android.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a soldering iron
hero_art.caption: OmniPython's mascot

displayif.title: displayif (moved) — OmniPython
displayif.headline: displayif has moved into omnipython-builds.
displayif.description: Moved to omnipython-builds as modules/displayif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by omnipython-builds' build.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

audiodsp.headline: audiodsp — CircuitPython-compatible audio for MicroPython and CPython.
audiodsp.description: CircuitPython's audio system (audiocore, synthio, audiomixer, effects, audiomp3) ported to MicroPython and CPython, extending CircuitPython along the way: dynamics, routing, convolution, and offline rendering. On PyPI as omnipython-audiodsp; the instrument and effect libraries built on it are audioinstruments and audioeffects.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a scope probe
hero_art.caption: Huey listens in on the signal

audioif.title: audioif (moved) — OmniPython
audioif.headline: audioif has moved into omnipython-builds.
audioif.description: Moved to omnipython-builds as modules/audioif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by omnipython-builds' build.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

audioinstruments.headline: audioinstruments — 33 playable synthesizers, organs, electric pianos and drum machines, in pure Python.
audioinstruments.description: Playable synthesizers, organs, electric pianos and drum machines, each a patch of modules on a virtual rack, rendered a block at a time on audiodsp. Pure Python on CPython and MicroPython-compatible firmware. Install omnipython-audioinstruments from PyPI, or audioinstruments from the MIP index.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a sparkler
hero_art.caption: Huey, ready to play

audioeffects.headline: audioeffects — 45 studio and guitar-pedal effects, in pure Python.
audioeffects.description: Compressors, EQs, reverbs, delays, modulation, drive and amp simulation, pitch shifters and racks, pure Python on audiodsp's audio nodes, the same on MicroPython-compatible boards, CircuitPython-compatible boards and a desktop. Install omnipython-audioeffects from PyPI, or audioeffects from the MIP index.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a wrench
hero_art.caption: Huey tightens up the sound

airwindows.headline: airwindows — 528 Airwindows plug-ins as audio nodes.
airwindows.description: Chris Johnson's Airwindows effects, reverbs, dynamics, filters, saturation and tape among them, ported to audiodsp's audio graph, the same on MicroPython-compatible firmware and CPython. Install omnipython-airwindows from PyPI, or build audioairwindows into your firmware beside audiodsp.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, hanging from a jumper wire
hero_art.caption: Huey lets the reverb tail ring

audiocomponents.title: audiocomponents (moved) — OmniPython
audiocomponents.headline: audiocomponents has split into audioinstruments and audioeffects.
audiocomponents.description: Split into two repositories: audioinstruments, the playable synthesizers, organs, electric pianos and drum machines, and audioeffects, the studio and guitar-pedal effects. Both are on PyPI and the MIP index, under the same names. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

usbif.title: usbif (moved) — OmniPython
usbif.headline: usbif has moved, to two homes.
usbif.description: The C module is now usbhost, in omnipython-builds as modules/usbhost (its binding is _usbhost, it was _usbif). The Python USB packages (usb.core, the host and device classes, usb-hid) are top-level packages in omnipython, installed with mip. Code that uses the packages doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

cameraif.title: cameraif (moved) — OmniPython
cameraif.headline: cameraif has moved into omnipython-builds.
cameraif.description: Moved to omnipython-builds as modules/cameraif, with its history. It was never published on its own: it reaches you in firmware built by omnipython-builds' build.py, so that is where it is built, tested and changed now. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

pygraphics.headline: pygraphics — 2D graphics engine & canvas framebuffer.
pygraphics.description: Native C and pure-Python 2D graphics library with drawing primitives, bitmap font rendering, paletted surface blitting, and area-dirtying pipelines.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a pencil
hero_art.caption: Huey draws

palettes.headline: palettes — Color math, wheels, cubes & swatch palettes.
palettes.description: Color management library with RGB565 / RGB888 output, an HSV color wheel, RGB color cubes, Material Design swatches, and Win16 color names.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a flower
hero_art.caption: Huey picks a colour

iconkit.headline: iconkit — Material Design icons for LVGL and pygraphics.
iconkit.description: Material Design icons as flash-resident alpha masks, drawn in LVGL or pygraphics.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a magnifying glass
hero_art.caption: Huey looks closely at small things

pdwidgets.headline: pdwidgets — a UI framework in Python, with no C.
pdwidgets.description: A complete UI widget framework in Python with no C: buttons, sliders, progress bars, labels and event routing on OmniPython screens. It demonstrates that the core can carry a UI framework; for an interface you ship, use LVGL. Not in release firmware: `mip install pdwidgets`.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a screwdriver
hero_art.caption: Huey puts the parts together

omnipython-lvgl.headline: omnipython-lvgl — LVGL v9 for MicroPython, CircuitPython and CPython.
omnipython-lvgl.description: LVGL v9 for Python: one binding generator turns LVGL's C headers into a MicroPython module, a CircuitPython module and a CPython wheel, so a program imports lvgl the same way on a desktop and on both kinds of board.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a circuit board
hero_art.caption: Huey with a board to light up

lvgl-bindings.title: lvgl-bindings (moved) — OmniPython
lvgl-bindings.headline: lvgl-bindings has moved into omnipython-lvgl.
lvgl-bindings.description: Moved to omnipython-lvgl as binding/, the generator that parses LVGL's C headers into the MicroPython, CircuitPython and CPython modules, with its history. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

lvgl-micropython.title: lvgl-micropython (moved) — OmniPython
lvgl-micropython.headline: lvgl-micropython has moved into omnipython-lvgl.
lvgl-micropython.description: Moved to omnipython-lvgl as its MicroPython port: build it into your firmware from the same repository that holds the generator. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

lvgl-python.title: lvgl-python (moved) — OmniPython
lvgl-python.headline: lvgl-python has moved into omnipython-lvgl.
lvgl-python.description: Moved to omnipython-lvgl as its CPython port. The wheels are omnipython-lvgl on PyPI. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

lvgl-circuitpython.title: lvgl-circuitpython (moved) — OmniPython
lvgl-circuitpython.headline: lvgl-circuitpython has moved into omnipython-lvgl.
lvgl-circuitpython.description: Moved to omnipython-lvgl as its CircuitPython port: build it into your firmware from the same repository that holds the generator. Your code doesn't change. The old repository is archived.

pyscript-template.headline: pyscript-template — Offline PWA starter template.
pyscript-template.description: Progressive Web App starter template repository for deploying offline-capable client-side OmniPython applications on GitHub Pages.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, on a jumper wire, holding a lit LED
hero_art.caption: Huey gets the first light on

android-template.headline: android-template — Android APK Buildozer project.
android-template.description: Pre-configured python-for-android build recipes and Buildozer project template for packaging OmniPython applications into native Android APKs.

mcuctl.headline: mcuctl — board tools for the editor, CLI, and agents.
mcuctl.description: Connect MicroPython and CircuitPython boards from VS Code, Cursor, or the CLI, over USB or Wi-Fi: dual-pane file transfer, in-editor REPL, firmware builds and flashing, mip/circup, plus RPC and an optional browser PWA.

gallery.headline: gallery — Showcase, demos & WebAssembly gallery.
gallery.description: Comprehensive example code, direct MicroPython WebAssembly demos, board configurations, and multi-interpreter showcase benchmarks.

gallery-pyscript.title: gallery — PyScript Gallery
gallery-pyscript.headline: PyScript Gallery
gallery-pyscript.description: Pyodide / PyScript demos that run full CPython in the browser — the same OmniPython examples as MCUs and the direct WebAssembly gallery. Explore drawing, input, widgets, and LVGL without flashing a board first.
gallery-pyscript.hero_note: Click a card to launch the app. The first load may take a few seconds while the interpreter downloads; featured demos stay pinned at the top.

PyDevices.github.io.headline: One Python program, on boards, desktops, browsers and phones.
PyDevices.github.io.description: OmniPython is a set of Python libraries and C modules that run unchanged on MicroPython, CircuitPython and CPython. Give each board or host a small board_config, and the same program drives its display, input and audio.
PyDevices.github.io.hero_note: Install it with pip on a desktop or omip on a board: the install page has the line for each. Or try it first, with nothing installed: the watch on this page is Python running in your browser, and every app in the gallery runs the same way.

hero_art.alt: Huey, a blue chameleon with lime spots, waving from a jumper wire
hero_art.caption: Huey, OmniPython's mascot

PyDevices.github.io.title: OmniPython: one Python program on boards, desktops, browsers and phones

omnipython-builds.headline: omnipython-builds — the versioned MicroPython runtime overlay.
omnipython-builds.description: The OmniPython patch queue for MicroPython, kept like a distribution keeps one: an ordered, provenance-tracked patch series over the pinned upstream (MicroPython v1.30.0-preview-160), with presets, boards and variants that build PyDevices modules into firmware with upstream's own make.

hero_art.alt: Huey, OmniPython's chameleon mascot, sitting on a jumper wire, waving
hero_art.caption: Huey waits for the build

workbench.headline: workbench — the browser IDE and MicroPython simulator.
workbench.description: A ViperIDE fork with a built-in WebAssembly MicroPython simulator: edit, run, and debug OmniPython code against a simulated board entirely in the browser, no hardware required.

mpvst.headline: mpvst — audio effects and instruments as a VST3 plug-in.
mpvst.description: Programmable VST3 instruments and effects: every audioinstruments instrument and audioeffects effect as a named plug-in, each instance running its Python in a sidecar process. Installers for Windows and Linux; nothing has to be built.

apps.headline: apps — Home, Watch and the apps they start.
apps.description: Finished apps for a board with a screen, or a desktop: Home and Watch to start them from, and apps for music, MIDI and audio, cameras and calls, the clock and the weather, remotes and the board itself, with the libraries they share. One omip line puts them all on a Wi-Fi board; pip puts them on a desktop.
